The Company

## Built Because GCs Deserved
a Glazing Sub That Actually Performed.

ACG was founded in South Florida on a straightforward premise: general contractors deserved a glazing subcontractor that operated with the same level of professionalism they brought to the job. Not a residential glass shop that occasionally takes commercial work. Not a sub that submits shop drawings when they get around to it and shows up to install when the schedule still works for them. A contractor, in the real sense of the word.

The commercial construction market in South Florida is demanding. Permitting is rigorous. Wind codes are among the strictest in the country. Building departments know the difference between a submittal that's been assembled by someone who understands the code and one that was thrown together to get through plan review. GCs working in this market have been burned enough times to know that the lowest-priced glazing bid is rarely the lowest-priced glazing scope when the job is done.

ACG grew from a single West Palm Beach office into a three-office Florida operation over the past 5+ years, delivering 350+ commercial projects across multifamily, hospitality, healthcare, retail, office, and institutional sectors. That growth happened because GCs who used ACG once came back for the next project — and the one after that. Read more about how we work with general contractors .

We're still a lean operation. No sprawling corporate structure. No accounts that get handed off to a junior rep after the contract is signed. The same people who bid your project are the people who deliver it.

What Makes ACG Different

## AI-Managed. Lean-Operated.
No Middlemen.

ACG uses AI-managed project operations — and it's worth being specific about what that means, because "AI" gets attached to a lot of things that don't deserve the label.

ACG's AI-managed system is a project management infrastructure that tracks every active job in real time across all three Florida offices. It isn't a chatbot. It isn't a marketing claim. It's the architecture that makes it possible for a lean team to manage a high volume of concurrent commercial projects without things falling through the cracks.

Real-Time Submittal Tracking
Every submittal is logged, tracked, and flagged when it's at risk of missing a deadline. Shop drawing schedules, AHJ review windows, material approval dependencies — all monitored without relying on a coordinator's memory.

Proactive Schedule Coordination
The system generates alerts when installation windows are approaching and preconditions haven't been confirmed. Your superintendent gets contacted by ACG before there's a problem — not after one has developed.

Material Procurement Tied to Approvals
Orders are placed against approved shop drawings, not assumed lead times. The system tracks material status from order to delivery and triggers proactive notification if a manufacturer's schedule changes.

Closeout Documentation Management
As-built drawings, FL Product Approval certificates, warranty documents, and lien waivers are tracked and assembled automatically as milestones are completed — not assembled at closeout from a pile of loose files.

Lean Management Model

ACG runs a flat management structure. When a project is awarded, a single project coordinator is assigned — and that person is your point of contact for shop drawings, submittals, material status, scheduling, and closeout. You're not calling a general office line and hoping someone picks up who knows your job.

There's no account manager who hands off to a project manager who hands off to a field supervisor who hands off to a crew chief. The coordinator knows the job because they've been on it from kickoff. When you have a question, you call the person who has the answer.

What GCs Get

48-hour scope turnaround from plan receipt

Single project coordinator — one call, one answer

Shop drawing submittals within 2–4 weeks of award

Proactive communication — not reactive updates

Florida PA and NOA documentation included standard

Self-performed installation — no sub-subs

Closeout package ready before final inspection

The Team

## Professional. Responsive.
Accountable.

ACG's team is built around a simple hiring standard: people who understand commercial construction, communicate proactively, and take ownership of the results. That's harder to find than it sounds in a trade where the default is to wait for the GC to ask before providing an update.

Project coordinators at ACG come from construction backgrounds — they've been on jobsites, they understand the language of a master schedule, they know what it means when your super says the openings won't be ready until next Tuesday. They're not order-processors reading from a script. They're construction people managing a scope.

Field crews are experienced commercial glaziers — not residential installers making a jump to commercial work. There's a meaningful difference between installing a residential window and installing a commercial curtainwall system to engineered shop drawings on a building with an occupied lower floor. ACG's crews understand that difference and are selected accordingly.

The culture ACG has built is straightforward: when something goes wrong — and in construction, something always eventually goes wrong — you tell the GC immediately, with a solution. Not after you've tried to fix it quietly and made it worse. Not after three emails asking for a status update. Immediately, in writing, with a path forward. GCs who've worked with ACG consistently mention this as the thing that separates us from the other glazing subs they've used.

Three Florida Offices

## Where ACG Operates.

Having local offices matters in commercial glazing. Local field crews, local supply relationships, and direct familiarity with local building departments make a meaningful difference in how smoothly a project runs.

Headquarters — Founded Here

West Palm Beach, FL

ACG's home base and founding market. South Florida's construction market is among the most technically demanding in the country — high wind speeds, complex permit processes, HVHZ compliance in southern areas, and a sophisticated GC community that expects genuine professionalism from their subs. ACG built its processes and standards here, and it shows in the work.

From West Palm Beach, ACG serves Palm Beach County, Broward County, Miami-Dade County, and the Treasure Coast — from Jupiter to Homestead and across the I-95 corridor. ACG also operates as a national commercial glazing contractor for GC partners who build outside Florida.

Southwest Florida Coverage

Naples, FL

Southwest Florida is a different market than South Florida — a mix of high-end residential-scale commercial, healthcare, hospitality, and the explosive growth along Collier, Lee, and Charlotte counties. The Naples office positions ACG to serve this corridor with local crews and direct familiarity with Collier County's building department processes.

Coverage extends through Fort Myers, Cape Coral, Bonita Springs, Marco Island, and across the Southwest Florida construction market. For complex coastal projects, proximity to the work matters.

Tampa Bay and I-75 Corridor

Tampa, FL

Tampa Bay is one of Florida's fastest-growing construction markets — Water Street Tampa, the Wesley Chapel commercial corridor, the suburban explosion in Brandon, Riverview, and east Hillsborough, and continued multifamily an

Code & Compliance

## Florida Building Code. Product approvals. NOA.

Every ACG-installed opening is engineered, submitted, and inspected against the governing Florida Building Code, including High-Velocity Hurricane Zone (HVHZ) requirements in Miami-Dade and Broward. Current product approvals and NOAs available on request for every manufacturer partner.

Full-Scope Glazing

# Every System.
One Sub.

Stop piecing together your glazing package from five different subs. ACG handles the complete scope — impact windows, storefronts, window wall, specialty systems — with one contract, one schedule, and one team that actually coordinates with your other trades.

01

### Impact Windows & Doors

HVHZ-rated impact systems engineered to meet or exceed Florida Building Code and large missile impact requirements.

Full range of impact window and door configurations. Laminated glass, structural silicone, thermal breaks. Certified hardware and installation methods. Meets the nation's most stringent hurricane protection codes.

Hurricane Rated
Impact Tested
FBC Approved
HVHZ

02

### Storefront Systems

Flush-glazed and thermally broken storefronts with custom finishes and architectural precision.

Commercial-grade framing systems with thermal performance and clean aesthetics. Anodized or powder-coated aluminum in custom colors. Seamless glazing from floor to ceiling, storefront entries, and tempered or laminated glass options.

Flush Glazed
Thermal Break
Custom Finishes
Commercial Grade

03

### Window Wall Systems

Slab-to-slab high-performance glazing systems for multifamily, hospitality, and mixed-use development.

Full curtainwall and window wall assemblies. Structural glazing or unitized systems. Impact-rated options for coastal markets. Thermal performance that exceeds code. Coordination with MEP trades and structural systems.

Slab-to-Slab
High Performance
Impact Rated
Unitized

04

### Sliding & Multi-Slide Doors

Multi-track pocket and stack-glass systems for seamless indoor-outdoor connectivity.

Heavy-duty aluminum framing with precision hardware. Pocket and stack configurations up to 20+ feet wide. Impact-rated options. Floor or pocket-mount installations. Full range of finishes and glass options.

Multi-Track
Pocket & Stack
Impact Rated
Wide Span

05

### Bifold Door Systems

Full-opening aluminum bifold systems that transform interior and exterior spaces.

Lightweight aluminum framing with heavy-duty tracks and rollers. Single or double-acting panels. Impact-rated glass options. Thermal breaks for energy efficiency. Contemporary hardware and custom finishes.

Full Opening
Aluminum Frames
Impact Options
Custom Hardware

06

### Fire-Rated Glass

UL-certified fire-rated glazing systems from 20 to 120 minutes.

Transparent and opaque fire-rated glass products. Life-safety rated framing systems. Integration with fire doors and building envelope requirements. Full compliance with IBC and local codes. ACG specializes in healthcare glazing and hospitality and country club glazing where fire-rated systems are a core requirement.

20-120 Min Rated
UL Certified
Life Safety
IBC Compliant

07

### Interior Glass Systems

Glass partitions, office fronts, and demising walls for modern interiors.

Frameless and framed partition systems. Acoustic and non-acoustic options. Switchable glass and privacy film. Custom hardware and finishes. Fire-rated interior glazing available.

Glass Partitions
Office Fronts
Custom Hardware
Acoustic Options

08

### Supply & Installation

Full project delivery from shop drawings through on-site installation and commissioning.

Coordination with architects, engineers, and general contractors. Plan review and constructability assessment. Shop drawing development and approval. Field installation with quality assurance. Punch-out and final commissioning.

Plan Review
Shop Drawings
Full Installation
Commissioning

FAQ

## Questions GCs ask before they bid.

Is Euro-Wall available in HVHZ / Miami-Dade NOA configurations? + Yes. Euro-Wall carries active Miami-Dade NOA on multiple configurations. ACG installs Euro-Wall in Miami-Dade, Broward, Palm Beach, Martin, Lee, and Collier counties. HVHZ-appropriate configuration is confirmed per project.

Can these systems handle Florida wind-driven rain? + Yes, when specified and installed correctly. Drainage is the entire game on multi-slide systems. ACG details the sill pan, drainage path, and threshold-to-interior-floor transition during shop-drawing phase — this is where most failures originate.

Folding vs. multi-slide vs. lift-and-slide — what's the difference? + Folding walls stack against one jamb in an accordion pattern (best for wide openings with a pocketing target). Multi-slide walls stack in overlapping tracks (best for medium openings). Lift-and-slide uses an oversized sliding mechanism where panels lift slightly to clear the sill on movement (best for very heavy single panels or luxury residential).

How long do these systems take to install? + Depends on configuration. A typical 20-ft folding wall with 6 panels: 3–4 days field install after rough opening is ready. Oversized lift-and-slide systems can take longer due to panel weight and mechanical alignment.

Does the Euro-Wall warranty apply to ACG installs? + Yes. Because ACG is an authorized Euro-Wall Florida dealer, the manufacturer warranty is intact on every system we install. Warranty service is coordinated through ACG and Euro-Wall directly.

OPEN

FAQ

## Questions GCs ask before they bid.

What is HVHZ and where does it apply? + HVHZ (High-Velocity Hurricane Zone) applies in Miami-Dade and Broward counties under the Florida Building Code. HVHZ requires impact-rated systems with active Miami-Dade NOA approvals. ACG is experienced in HVHZ submittal and installation protocols and carries manufacturer NOAs on every HVHZ project.

What is a DP rating? + DP (Design Pressure) rating specifies the structural and water-resistance capacity of a window or door system at a given building elevation. Higher floors and coastal exposures require higher DP ratings. ACG engineers DP-appropriate system selection from shop-drawing phase forward.

What is the difference between impact and hurricane-rated? + "Impact" means the system has passed large-missile impact testing (ASTM E1886/E1996). "Hurricane-rated" is a more general marketing term. For code compliance in Florida — especially HVHZ — the spec should always say "impact-rated" and reference the NOA or Florida Product Approval.

Can ACG supply impact glazing for a GC in a non-HVHZ county? + Yes. Florida Product Approval applies statewide. We install impact glazing in Lee, Collier, Palm Beach, Martin, St. Lucie, Hillsborough, Pinellas, and every county between.

How long are typical lead times on commercial impact systems? + Standard impact storefront runs 6–10 weeks from approved shop drawings. Large-missile tested window wall 8–12 weeks. Custom impact sliders 10–14 weeks. ACG confirms firm lead times with a bid submission.

Ground-Up vs Retrofit

## Why New Construction Is a
Different Scope.

New construction glazing is not a larger version of retrofit work. The submittal chain is longer, the coordination with adjacent trades is tighter, and the permitting path requires engineered documentation in hand before fabrication starts. Here's how ACG approaches ground-up Division 08 differently from an existing-building scope.

Full Submittal Workflow

On retrofit, dimensions come off a field measure. On new construction, every opening starts from architectural drawings — takeoff, shop drawings, engineering calculations, and Florida-licensed PE-stamped submittals go through the GC and architect before fabrication begins.

Trade Coordination

Framing tolerances, envelope waterproofing, roofing tie-ins, and interior finishes all meet the glazing scope at the rough opening. ACG sequences buck-out, flashing laps, and perimeter sealant details with the GC's framers, waterproofers, and roofers in the field.

NOA & Engineering

Every exterior opening on a Florida commercial new-build needs a Florida Product Approval number — or a Miami-Dade NOA inside HVHZ. ACG assembles the full approval package, site-specific wind load calculations per ASCE 7-22, and PE-stamped shop drawings for permit.

Pre-Glazed Storefront

ACG's signature advantage: pre-glazed storefront arrives at the jobsite as complete, factory-assembled units. Field install rate runs around 1,000 SF per day per crew versus roughly 500 SF per day for stick-built. Quality is also more consistent because seals are set in factory conditions.

Finish Lead Times

Standard factory finishes — clear anodized, dark bronze anodized, Kynar AAMA 2605 in stock colors — ship on normal lead times. Custom Kynar color matches, two-tone finishes, or specialty anodized runs add 2 – 4 weeks. ACG flags finish schedule impact at takeoff so GCs can trade scope against schedule.

Buck-Out & Flashing

On new construction, the rough opening, sub-sill pan, and head flashing are all coordinated before frame arrives. ACG provides buck-out details on shop drawings so the framers and waterproofers have exact dimensions and material requirements, eliminating the field adjustments that create warranty exposure later.

What's in Scope

## Division 08 Systems on a
New Construction Commercial Project.

01

#### Impact Windows (HVHZ + LMI)

Large Missile Impact windows tested to TAS 201/202/203 for HVHZ counties, or ASTM E1886/E1996 Large Missile for Florida Product Approval elsewhere. Punched openings, ribbon windows, and architectural configurations.

02

#### Storefront Systems

Pre-glazed aluminum storefront — ESWindows ES-8000 and similar platforms — at typical install rate of 1,000 SF per day per crew. Thermally broken options for energy code. Medium-stile and heavy-stile entrances in the same system.

03

#### Curtainwall

Stick-built curtainwall for mid-rise, or unitized systems like the ESWindows GW-7000 for high-rise and aggressive schedules. Structural silicone glazed and captured configurations. Engineered to ASCE 7-22 wind design pressures.

04

#### Entry Door Systems

Impact-rated commercial entrances, including ESWindows ES-9000 medium-stile pairs and Euro-Wall folding entry configurations. Offset pivots, continuous gear hinges, full commercial hardware packages.

05

#### Sliding Glass Doors

Impact sliding glass doors — ESWindows ES-SGD2020, Euro-Wall Vista Multi Slide, and equivalent platforms. OX, XO, OXO, and OXXO panel configurations in two-, three-, and four-panel layouts for multifamily and hospitality openings.

06

#### Interior Glass

Frameless and framed interior partitions, conference room office fronts, demountable glass walls, and acoustic interior glazing where STC ratings are specified for office or medical tenant buildouts.

07

#### Skylights & Glass Railings

Structurally glazed skylights where specified on roof plans, and structural glass railings for balconies, stairs, and mezzanines. ASTM E2353 impact testing and railing load compliance per IBC 1607.

08

#### Folding Glass Walls

Euro-Wall folding systems and multi-slide systems for restaurants, hospitality, and indoor/outdoor commercial spaces. Impact-rated where required by code and exposure.

From Award to Closeout

## The New Construction
Workflow.

A typical ground-up commercial glazing scope runs 12 to 20 weeks from award to completed install, depending on system complexity and finish lead times. Here's how ACG sequences the work.

01

#### Plans Review & Takeoff

1 – 2 weeks. ACG reviews architectural, structural, and envelope drawings, runs a full quantity takeoff, flags spec conflicts, and returns a line-item proposal. Standard bid turnaround is 48 hours on most commercial scopes.

02

#### Shop Drawings & Engineering

2 – 3 weeks. In-house shop drawings developed from CDs — elevations, details, anchor schedules, wind load calculations per ASCE 7-22, and Florida-licensed PE stamps for permit. Coordinated with the architect and GC throughout.

03

#### Submittals & NOA Documentation

1 – 2 weeks. Florida Product Approval references or Miami-Dade NOA packages assembled for every exterior opening. Glass specs, sealant data, hardware cuts, and finish samples routed through the submittal workflow.

04

#### Factory Fabrication

4 – 8 weeks. Depending on system. Storefront and standard impact windows run on the shorter end; custom curtainwall, specialty entrances, and non-standard finishes run longer. ACG tracks fabrication against the GC's install milestones weekly.

05

#### Field Install

GC-coordinated schedule. Pre-glazed storefront installs at roughly 1,000 SF per day per crew. Stick-built curtainwall and large unit glazing sequenced against the envelope schedule. Perimeter sealants, glazing punch list, and closeout documentation follow install.

The Specification Standard

## What Division 08
Covers.

In commercial construction, the CSI MasterFormat system organizes every scope of work into numbered divisions. Division 08 is Openings — and it covers everything that fills a penetration in a building's envelope or interior structure.

The Division 08 specification sections on a typical commercial project include: Section 081100 (Metal Doors and Frames), Section 083100 (Access Doors), Section 084113 (Aluminum-Framed Entrances and Storefronts), Section 084200 (Entrances), Section 086000 (Skylights), Section 088000 (Glazing), and Section 087000 (Door Hardware). The exact sections in scope depend on the project's design and the architect's spec.

For a GC, Division 08 represents a significant portion of the building enclosure — and one of the most technically complex procurement challenges on any project. Systems must be engineered to meet structural loads, thermal performance requirements, and Florida Building Code wind ratings, all while coordinating with the structural frame, roofing, and interior finishes.

That's why GCs who need Division 08 done right — without splits, gaps, or finger-pointing between subs — turn to ACG.

Division 08 Sections ACG Covers

08 41 13

Aluminum Storefront & Entrances

08 44 13

Glazed Aluminum Curtainwall

08 43 00

Storefronts & Window Wall

08 88 00

Special Function Glazing (Impact, FR)

08 42 13

Automatic Entrance Doors

08 70 00

Hardware & Access Control Rough-In

08 34 00

Fire-Rated Glass Assemblies

Why One Sub for All of Division 08

When Division 08 scope is split across multiple subs — one for glass, one for hardware, one for doors — coordination failures happen at the seam. A single sub owns every opening and every interface. No gaps. No blame-shifting.

Scope Consolidation

## Why GCs Need a Dedicated
Division 08 Sub — Not a Split.

When Division 08 scope is broken apart — a glazing sub for windows, a door supplier for frames, a hardware dealer for closers and locksets — GCs absorb the coordination risk at every interface. Who owns the rough opening tolerances? Who's responsible when the door frame doesn't align with the storefront system? Who's on the hook for the wind load calculation at the threshold connection?

The answer in a split-scope arrangement is rarely clear. And in Florida, where the Florida Building Code demands fully engineered, product-approved assemblies for every opening, the legal and liability exposure is real.

A dedicated Division 08 glazing contractor absorbs all of that. One submittal package covers every opening. One field crew sequences every installation. One point of contact answers the phone when the inspector shows up.

ACG provides a complete, consolidated Division 08 scope. From the moment you send plans, we take ownership of every opening in the building — the storefront at grade, the curtainwall above, the impact windows in the units, the fire-rated glass in the stairwell, the automatic sliding doors at the lobby.

Our submittal package covers all sections simultaneously. Our AI-managed scheduling sequences every opening against your master schedule, not against our convenience. And our 48-hour scope turnaround means you can close your budget without waiting two weeks for a proposal.

Florida Building Code

## Division 08 in Florida
Is Different. Harder.

Florida's building code environment makes Division 08 more complex than any other state. Every product installed in an exterior opening must carry a Florida Product Approval number — or a Miami-Dade Notice of Acceptance (NOA) for High-Velocity Hurricane Zone (HVHZ) projects in Broward and Miami-Dade counties.

Florida Building Code Section 1609 governs wind load design for all structures. Every glazing system — storefront, curtainwall, window wall, impact windows — must be designed and tested to resist the design wind pressures at the specific building height and location. Coastal exposure categories (B, C, D) further influence the required performance levels. In the HVHZ, Miami-Dade County maintains its own enhanced testing and approval protocol that exceeds the base Florida code.

Florida Product Approval for every exterior opening

Miami-Dade NOA compliance for HVHZ projects

Wind exposure category analysis per ASCE 7

FBC Chapter 14 (Exterior Walls) coordination

Engineer-of-record submittal coordination

Shop drawings stamped by Florida-licensed PE

Florida Wind Speed Zones

HVHZ (Miami-Dade / Broward)
185+ mph

South Florida Coastal
165–180 mph

Gulf Coast (Naples / Ft. Myers)
150–165 mph

Tampa Bay Coastal
130–150 mph

Central Florida (Inland)
120–130 mph

Design wind speeds per ASCE 7-22 / Florida Building Code 8th Edition. Actual values vary by location, exposure category, and building height.

Background

Connor Walsh is the President of American Commercial Glass. He holds Florida Certified General Contractor license CGC #1531993 — the credential required to legally pull permits for commercial glazing scopes in the State of Florida.

Before founding ACG in 2020 with his wife Rielly Walsh, Connor flew commercial jets professionally. A 2017 traumatic brain injury ended his aviation career and pulled him back into construction full-time. He founded Liberty Impact in 2014, scaling it from $400K to $10M in annual revenue before selling. He also founded GoGym , a portable training company, and completed the 75 Hard mental toughness program twice.

At ACG, Connor authors the technical content on acglass.com — the Florida code reference articles, the glazing system comparisons, the bid-process guides. The work is reviewed against Florida Building Code 2023, Miami-Dade NOA criteria, and ACG's 350+ project field data.

Connor is a member of Arete Syndicate , an executive growth community led by Andy Frisella and Ed Mylett.

Background

Rielly Walsh is the CEO of American Commercial Glass. She holds a BS in Concrete Industry Management from Middle Tennessee State University — one of the few college programs anywhere that trains concrete and structural professionals from a materials-up perspective.

Her concrete-and-stone background is the unusual edge in glazing leadership: most exterior envelope executives have never worked the structure from the other side. Rielly has. She reads a building the way the GC does — in layers, sequences, and interfaces. The peak in the field, walking Panther National with the Verdex team, is the photo that captures her job.

Rielly joined ACG in 2022 to launch the company into its current chapter. She owns strategy and long-term vision — the Naples and Tampa office expansions, the AI-managed operations stack that distinguishes ACG from legacy subcontractors, and the manufacturer-partner relationships with ESWindows and Euro-Wall.

The complication: all of it is HVHZ. Every project in Broward County — from a ground-floor Las Olas restaurant storefront to a multi-story Weston corporate campus — requires glazing systems with Miami-Dade NOA documentation. Most Florida glazing subs can handle standard FL-approval work. Far fewer maintain the HVHZ-compliant product inventories and submittal expertise required in Broward County.

ACG's West Palm Beach headquarters is approximately 40 miles north of Fort Lauderdale. We've maintained active project presence in Broward County for years, with completed projects including CubeSmart Davie and Ocean Prime Fort Lauderdale . We know the county's building department, we understand the permitting rhythm, and our AI-managed scheduling keeps Broward projects on timeline despite the documentation complexity that HVHZ work demands. We also serve Delray Beach and Boynton Beach in the surrounding region.

HVHZ in Broward County

## Why HVHZ Experience Matters
for Broward GCs.

Broward County is entirely within Florida's High Velocity Hurricane Zone (HVHZ) — the same designation that covers all of Miami-Dade County. For GCs bidding and building in Fort Lauderdale, this is the single most important compliance factor in the glazing scope. A glazing sub without proven HVHZ documentation experience will cost you time, money, and plan review re-submissions.

The core requirement: every glazing system installed in Broward County needs Miami-Dade NOA (Notice of Acceptance) — not just a Florida Product Approval (FL#). NOA approval is issued by Miami-Dade County's Building Code Compliance Office (BCCO) and requires testing under TAS (Testing Application Standard) protocols. TAS 201 tests large missile impact resistance; TAS 202 tests uniform static air pressure; TAS 203 tests cyclic wind pressure loading. These protocols exceed the ASTM test standards used for standard FL approvals.

The failure mode ACG frequently inherits: a glazing sub awarded the Broward County scope shows up with materials carrying only FL approval numbers. Broward plan review flags the documentation as insufficient for HVHZ. Re-submittal takes weeks. The project schedule slips. The GC takes the pain. ACG prevents this — our submittal packages are NOA-compliant from day one, built specifically for Broward County plan review standards.

HVHZ Compliance Checklist

-
&#10003;
Miami-Dade NOA numbers for all installed systems

-
&#10003;
TAS 201/202/203 test reports on file

-
&#10003;
Engineer-of-record signed & sealed shop drawings

-
&#10003;
Wind load calculations per ASCE 7 and FBC HVHZ

-
&#10003;
Anchor design per manufacturer's NOA conditions

-
&#10003;
Broward County plan review submission-ready package

ACG NOA-Compliant Systems

- ESWindows — Commercial aluminum impact; Miami-Dade NOA to TAS 201/202/203

- ESWindows — Commercial series; current NOA for mid-rise and high-rise

- Slimpact — Narrow-profile impact; NOA with slender sight-line aesthetics

- PGT — Curtainwall and storefront; HVHZ-compliant series with NOA documentation

## Southwest Florida's Most
Demanding Construction Market.

Naples is one of the wealthiest markets in the United States — and one of the most unforgiving for commercial glazing contractors who come unprepared. The luxury residential and commercial projects along Fifth Avenue South, the Mercato mixed-use district on Vanderbilt Beach Road, and the resort-grade construction throughout Pelican Bay and Park Shore demand glazing work that holds up architecturally and performs against some of Florida's most extreme coastal wind and salt air exposure.

ACG has a permanent Naples office. That means local field crews, established relationships with Collier County building officials, and project managers who know the local subcontractor ecosystem — not a West Palm Beach sub making two-hour drives across Alligator Alley. When a superintendent needs a field decision at 7 AM, ACG's Naples team is reachable. When a punch item surfaces during a CO inspection, our crew is there the same day.

The healthcare sector in Collier County is growing at a pace that outstrips most Florida markets. NCH Baker Hospital's expansion program, Physicians Regional's campuses on Pine Ridge Road and Collier Boulevard, and the broader medical office corridor that follows North Naples residential growth all represent multi-year glazing work for contractors who can execute to hospital-grade submittal and schedule standards.

Beyond Naples proper, the Estero corridor and Ave Maria represent the fastest-growing commercial construction submarkets in Lee and Collier Counties. Siena Lakes Naples, Estero Vista, Imperial Crossings, and the Causeway Building Bonita Springs are among the projects ACG has completed in this market — evidence that our Southwest Florida footprint is operational, not aspirational.

## Euro-Wall Installer Florida
Source: https://acglass.com/euro-wall-installer-florida.html

American Commercial Glass (ACG) is a Florida-based authorized installer of Euro-Wall systems, including the SGD2020 multi-slide door, Vistafold folding door, and Euro-Wall pivot systems. ACG has installed Euro-Wall on landmark projects including Panther National Clubhouse (Palm Beach Gardens), Eau Palm Beach Resort (Manalapan), and Atlantic Fields (Hobe Sound). License: FL CGC #1531993.

American Commercial Glass — acglass.com/euro-wall-installer-florida.html — FL CGC #1531993

Euro-Wall Product Lines

## Four systems. One authorized installer.

ACG installs the full Euro-Wall commercial door lineup. Each system has a distinct structural and performance role. ACG matches system to opening, not the other way around.

Sliding System

### Euro-Wall SGD2020 Multi-Slide

Thermally broken aluminum multi-slide door system for wide commercial openings. Panels stack in opposing tracks to create a fully open wall plane. Used by ACG on country club amenity buildings, resort indoor-outdoor dining, and waterfront restaurants. Carries Florida Product Approval and Miami-Dade NOA on applicable configurations.

Folding System

### Vistafold Folding Doors

Accordion-style folding wall that pockets flush to the jamb when fully open. Flush-threshold profile for barrier-free transitions to exterior decks and pool areas. ACG uses Vistafold where the opening needs to disappear entirely — dining rooms that open onto terraces, clubhouse bars with outdoor seating, and resort cabana buildings.

Pivot System

### Pivot Doors

Oversized single-panel pivot door systems with concealed floor and ceiling pivots. Used at primary entries where architectural scale is required — clubhouse main entries, resort lobbies, private club arrival sequences. Panel heights to 14 ft and beyond. ACG coordinates pivot hardware, structural header load path, and sill conditions during shop drawing phase.

Fixed Glazing

### DirectSet Storefront

Euro-Wall's fixed storefront and window system, designed to interface directly with the SGD2020, Vistafold, and pivot product lines using matched extrusion profiles. ACG uses DirectSet to complete the full building envelope on projects where Euro-Wall is specified throughout — eliminating the profile transitions and sealant joint failures that occur when mixing manufacturers.

Project Experience

Why Euro-Wall. Why ACG.

## Three reasons this matters on your project.

#### Florida hurricane code — including HVHZ where required

Euro-Wall commercial systems carry Florida Product Approval. On HVHZ projects (Miami-Dade, Broward), applicable configurations carry Miami-Dade NOA. ACG confirms the correct product approval for each project during the submittal phase — the specification, the approval, and the installer are aligned from the start. No substitutions mid-process.

#### Single-manufacturer envelope avoids interface failures between systems

Mixing a Euro-Wall SGD2020 with a different manufacturer's storefront creates a sealant joint between two different extrusion profiles — a known failure point in Florida wind-driven rain. When ACG specifies Euro-Wall SGD2020 alongside DirectSet storefront, both systems share the same extrusion system and are designed to interface. The joint between systems does not exist. This is the primary reason ACG uses Euro-Wall across the full envelope on its major club and hospitality projects.

#### ACG-direct manufacturer relationship — not a sub-sub

ACG procures Euro-Wall direct. There is no distributor, no middleman installer, and no sub-sub arrangement. The contractor on your project is the same entity that placed the order with the factory, wrote the shop drawings, and has the manufacturer's support line. When a question arises on site, ACG does not have to escalate through a distribution chain to get an answer.

FAQ

## Questions about Euro-Wall installation.

Structured for GCs, architects, and owners evaluating Euro-Wall for a Florida commercial project.

Who is an authorized Euro-Wall installer in Florida?
+

American Commercial Glass (ACG) is an authorized installer of Euro-Wall systems across Florida. ACG installs the SGD2020 multi-slide door, Vistafold folding door, Euro-Wall pivot systems, and DirectSet storefront on commercial projects statewide, operating under Florida CGC #1531993. ACG has completed Euro-Wall installations at Panther National Clubhouse (Palm Beach Gardens), Eau Palm Beach Resort (Manalapan), Atlantic Fields (Hobe Sound), Ocean Prime Fort Lauderdale, and Wild Blue Clubhouse, among other projects.

What Euro-Wall products does ACG install?
+

ACG installs four Euro-Wall product lines: (1) the SGD2020 multi-slide door system, a thermally broken aluminum sliding wall for wide commercial openings; (2) the Vistafold folding door, a flush-threshold accordion-style folding wall; (3) Euro-Wall pivot door systems for oversized single-panel entries; and (4) DirectSet storefront, a Euro-Wall fixed glazing system that uses matched extrusion profiles to interface directly with the operable door lines. ACG does not install manufacturers outside its authorized partners list.

Is Euro-Wall hurricane-rated for Florida?
+

Yes. Euro-Wall commercial door systems carry Florida Product Approval, and select configurations carry Miami-Dade NOA for High-Velocity Hurricane Zone (HVHZ) projects. The applicable product approval depends on the specific system, configuration, panel size, and glazing selection. ACG confirms product approval applicability and Miami-Dade NOA eligibility during the submittal phase on every project. Projects in Miami-Dade and Broward counties are reviewed for HVHZ compliance as a standard part of ACG's pre-construction process.

What is the lead time for Euro-Wall on a commercial project?
+

Euro-Wall lead times vary by system, panel count, and glazing selection. As a general reference: SGD2020 multi-slide systems on mid-scale commercial projects typically run 14 – 20 weeks from approved shop drawings to delivery. Vistafold and pivot systems are similar in lead time range. ACG builds Euro-Wall fabrication lead time into the project schedule during the pre-construction phase and coordinates fabrication kickoff against the GC's projected framing completion date to avoid delivery ahead of rough opening readiness.

Does ACG handle the structural opening prep, or just install?
+

ACG's scope is the Euro

ESWindows Commercial Product Line

## Three core systems. One authorized installer.

ESWindows manufactures a full commercial aluminum envelope. ACG installs the three systems that appear most often on Florida commercial specifications: the ES8000 storefront, the ES50 commercial window line, and the ES Curtainwall.

Storefront System

### ES8000 Storefront

The ES8000 is ESWindows' primary DirectSet aluminum storefront for ground-floor and 2-story commercial construction. Pre-glazed with screw-spline construction, it accepts an integral ES-9000 door adaptor and carries active Miami-Dade NOA for Large Missile Impact applications. Standard in retail, medical, office, and institutional envelopes across Florida.

### ES50 Window Line

With a 5-inch stile width and LMI + SMI impact ratings, the ES50 handles the structural and impact demands of Florida's coastal commercial market. Coordinates with ES8000 storefront systems as the entrance component.

The ES-7525 stick curtainwall carries LMI + SMI impact ratings plus blast resistance (GSA Condition 2). The GW-7000 unitized curtainwall is Miami-Dade certified for LMI + SMI at DP +100/&#8209;140 psf. ACG installs both systems on office, hospitality, and government envelopes.

Stick-built and unitized configurations

Why ESWindows on Florida Commercial Projects

## What makes ESWindows the right specification.

Florida commercial projects carry compliance obligations that eliminate systems without the right approvals. ESWindows and ACG together cover those requirements without piecemeal sourcing.

Miami-Dade NOA + FBC Product Approvals
ESWindows products carry active Miami-Dade Notice of Acceptance (NOA) numbers across the storefront, window wall, and curtainwall lines. ACG manages the NOA submittal process and coordinates the product approval documentation required under the Florida Building Code for HVHZ-permitted projects in Miami-Dade and Broward counties.

Thermal Performance and Impact Ratings for HVHZ
The ES8000T thermally broken storefront (NOA 21-0914.03, exp. Aug 2031) and the GW-7000 unitized curtainwall both satisfy the concurrent thermal and hurricane-impact requirements that apply to Florida commercial projects — particularly ENERGY STAR-governed occupancies and LEED-targeted hotel and multifamily builds.

Single-Manufacturer Envelope vs. Piecemeal Scope
Specifying ESWindows for storefront, window wall, and curtainwall across a single project produces system-to-system coordination from one manufacturer's engineering team. Mullion profiles, thermal break geometry, and finish programs align across product categories, which reduces RFI exposure and simplifies the submittals package.

ACG's Direct ESWindows Commercial Relationship
ACG's standing as an authorized ESWindows installer means project pricing, lead-time coordination, and technical support flow through a direct channel — not a distributor layer. For Florida commercial schedules where glazing procurement lead time is on the critical path, this direct relationship matters.

Florida Code & HVHZ Compliance

## HVHZ, wind load, and NOA — what it actually means.

The High-Velocity Hurricane Zone (HVHZ) designation applies to Miami-Dade and Broward counties under the Florida Building Code. Every glazing system installed in HVHZ must carry a Miami-Dade Notice of Acceptance or Florida Product Approval with verified impact test results. ACG handles the submittal and coordination process for ESWindows systems on HVHZ projects.

#### HVHZ Counties and Wind Load Requirements

Miami-Dade and Broward counties require that fenestration products be tested and listed under an active Miami-Dade NOA. Wind speed design criteria in HVHZ typically exceeds 170 mph (Exposure D per ASCE 7). Design pressures for glazing in HVHZ commercial projects commonly range from &#8209;60 psf to &#8209;130 psf depending on building height, roof zone, and wall zone classification. ESWindows ES8000 is rated to DP +130/&#8209;130 psf LMI.

Miami-Dade NOA
HVHZ Compliant
FBC Chapter 17

#### Impact Testing: ASTM E1996 and ASTM E1886

Products in HVHZ must pass ASTM E1886 (impact test method) and ASTM E1996 (performance specification for missile impact). Large Missile Impact (LMI) applies to floors 1–3 and uses a 9-pound 2x4 lumber missile at 50 ft/s. Small Missile Impact (SMI) applies at floor 4 and above, using 10 steel ball bearings at 130 ft/s. ESWindows ES8000, ES-7525, and GW-7000 all carry LMI ratings. ACG coordinates the impact test documentation required for permit submittals in HVHZ jurisdictions.

ASTM E1996
ASTM E1886
LMI / SMI Rated

#### Active ESWindows NOA Numbers (ACG Projects)

ACG submits the applicable NOA documentation with each HVHZ permit package. Key ESWindows NOAs in ACG's active project portfolio:

- NOA 24-0321.07 — ES8000 Storefront, LMI, exp. Apr 2028

- NOA 21-0914.03 — ES8000T Thermal Storefront, LMI, exp. Aug 2031

- NOA 23-0724.09 — ES-7000 Window Wall, LMI, exp. Jul 2028

- GW-7000 — Unitized Curtainwall, Miami-Dade certified, LMI + SMI

#### ACG Handles the NOA Submittal Process

For HVHZ projects, ACG prepares the product approval package including the applicable ESWindows NOA, glazing specs, and installation drawings stamped to meet Miami-Dade HVHZ permit requirements. This removes the burden from the GC's project manager and reduces the risk of a glazing hold-up during permit review. ACG's three Florida offices (West Palm Beach, Naples, Tampa) maintain active relationships with the applicable building departments across the state.
